Repo: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa, branch feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component.

REWORK round 1 of 3 on Step 4 (ZimmProductCardMedia molecule) of the SFCC-236 build. The Scorer independently reproduced two real defects via live mutation testing and authorized five specific, bounded fixes. Do ONLY these five. Stay inside the existing 4 files (`index.tsx`, `index.stories.tsx`, `index.test.tsx`, `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`) — no new files, no other component touched.

## Fix 1 — structural test proving arrows/indicator mutual exclusivity
File: `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/index.test.tsx`.

The Scorer proved this component's DOM-level tests give zero protection here: they deleted the `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY` media-query gate entirely from the recipe (making arrows permanently visible regardless of pointer capability) and the ENTIRE 21-test suite still passed, because `useMultiStyleConfig` is mocked to `{}` for every part — the real CSS is never exercised.

Fix: add ONE new test that imports the REAL, unmocked recipe module directly (`import { ZimmProductCardMedia as ZimmProductCardMediaRecipe } from './zimmProductCardMedia.css'` — check the actual export name in that file) and calls `.baseStyle(...)` with representative props, then asserts that within the SAME media-query key (the `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` block), the `carousel` part's `display` and the `indicatorWrapper` part's `display` resolve to values that can never both be visible at once (e.g. one is `'flex'`/`'block'` and the other is `'none'` inside that media block, and vice versa outside it, however your recipe actually structures the conditional — read the recipe file first to know its exact shape before writing the assertion).

**Two live, shipped precedents for this exact "test the real recipe object directly, bypass the useMultiStyleConfig mock" technique already exist in this repo** — read both before writing this test: `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmSizeChip/zimmSizeChip.css.test.ts` and `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmTextInput/zimmTextInput.css.test.ts`. Match their pattern exactly (a plain unit test on the exported style-resolver/baseStyle function, no Chakra/DOM/render involved).

After writing the test, prove it's real: temporarily reintroduce the Scorer's mutation (delete/neutralise the media-query gate in the recipe), confirm THIS NEW test now fails, then revert and confirm it passes again.

## Fix 2 — missing focus-visible outline on two interactive overlays
File: `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`.

The `close` and `arrowButton` recipe parts have zero `_focusVisible` styling — both are real native `<button>` overlays on top of photographic images with only the bare browser-default outline on keyboard focus. Add, to BOTH parts:
```ts
_focusVisible: {
  outline: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring)',
  outlineOffset: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)',
},
```
This is the exact pair already used identically in `zimmColourSwatch.css.ts:28-29`, `zimmNavItem.css.ts:47-49`, and `zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts:174-176` — copy the precedent exactly, don't invent a new value.

**Do NOT add `_hover`** — there is no Figma citation for a hover treatment on either element, and inventing one would be scope creep beyond what this fix authorizes.

Add a test (or extend an existing focus-related test if one exists) asserting the recipe's `close`/`arrowButton` parts include this `_focusVisible` block — same "test the real recipe object" technique as Fix 1, or a DOM-level `getComputedStyle`-adjacent check if that's more natural given how the rest of this file's tests are structured; use your judgement on which fits, but it must exercise the REAL recipe, not the mock.

## Fix 3 — stale currentIndex not re-clamped when images prop shrinks
File: `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/index.tsx`.

Confirmed bug, reproduced live by the Scorer: mount with a 3-image gallery, navigate to the last image (index 2), then re-render the SAME instance with a 2-image gallery (e.g. a colour-variant swap while the card stays mounted) — the component's internal `currentIndex` state stays at the stale value `2`. `ZimmSlideIndicator`'s own display-side clamp masks this visually right after the shrink (it happens to show "2 of 2", which looks fine), but the next click on "Next" is then a silent no-op — it takes TWO clicks to actually advance, because the navigation math (`goToRelativeSlide`, around line 136-141) computes from the stale unclamped value.

Fix: add a clamp effect, shaped after the precedent already in this exact codebase — read `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx:75-84` first (its own comment explains: "clamp to the highest valid page so all remaining swatches stay visible after the offered set shrinks"). Add an equivalent `useEffect` here that re-clamps `currentIndex` whenever the `images`/gallery array's length changes such that the current index would be out of range, keyed on whatever dependency array correctly captures "the slide count changed."

Add a regression test: mount with 3 images, navigate to the last, rerender with 2 images, click "Next" ONCE, assert the indicator now correctly reads "Image 1 of 2" (i.e. wrapped correctly on the FIRST click post-shrink, not the second).

## Fix 4 — zero test coverage on the scrollend listener
File: `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/index.test.tsx`.

The `scrollend` event listener (around lines 149-161) drives the touch-only slide indicator's accuracy — real, non-trivial clamping logic with zero coverage today. Add at least one test that:
- Mounts the component with a multi-image gallery.
- Dispatches a real `scrollend` event on the scroll container (`container.querySelector('[data-card-slot="..."]').dispatchEvent(new Event('scrollend'))` — use whichever `data-card-slot` value is actually the scroll container per this file's own documented contract).
- Before dispatching, set the container's `scrollLeft`/`clientWidth`/`scrollWidth` via `Object.defineProperty` (jsdom doesn't lay these out for real, but they ARE definable properties, confirmed working by the Scorer) to simulate "scrolled to image 2 of 3."
- Asserts the indicator's `activeIndex`/accessible label updates to reflect that scroll position.

## Fix 5 — minimal, additive keyboard operability on the scroll container (WCAG 2.1.1 gap)
This is the most important fix. Currently: `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` gates VISUAL affordance (arrows vs. indicator) correctly, but a device that resolves this query false — a touchscreen with a physical keyboard attached, a switch-access user, or simply a desktop browser reporting `hover:none` — has NO way to page a multi-image gallery via keyboard at all today. Arrows are `display:none` (unreachable), the indicator has zero focusable content (confirmed: `ZimmSlideIndicator` is a non-interactive `role="group"` div with `aria-hidden` children), and the scroll container itself has no `tabIndex`/`onKeyDown`.

**This fix is strictly additive and must not touch the existing visual hover/touch CSS split at all** — same `carousel`/`indicatorWrapper` display logic stays exactly as-is. You are ONLY making the underlying scroll container keyboard-operable, regardless of pointer capability, as a parallel, always-available operability layer underneath whatever's visually shown.

Precise required shape — do not build beyond this:
1. `tabIndex={0}` on the scroll container element, gated on `totalSlides > 1` (the SAME condition the indicator already uses — NOT gated on `showControls`, so this works even when `showControls={false}`).
2. `onKeyDown` handler on that same element: `ArrowLeft` calls the same navigation function the visible arrows already call for "previous" (`goToRelativeSlide(-1)` or equivalent — use whatever the existing function is actually named), `ArrowRight` calls the equivalent "next". Call `event.preventDefault()` for exactly these two keys, matching the pattern already used in `zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx:109-111` (read it for the exact idiom).
3. One new `defineMessages` entry for an `aria-label` on this container, matching the naming/message-id convention of this file's existing `previousImage`/`nextImage` messages (check the actual message IDs already in the file and follow the same `product_card_media.*`-shaped namespace). Add `role="group"` to the container (matches `ZimmSlideIndicator`'s own choice of role for a similar non-native-widget grouping).
4. A `_focusVisible` outline on the scroll-container's own recipe part (`var(--zimm-focus-ring)` / `var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)`, same pair as Fix 2) — this is a direct, mandatory consequence of making the element focusable, not a separate design decision.
5. One test mirroring this file's existing "arrows wrap at both ends" test, but firing via `fireEvent.keyDown(container, {key: 'ArrowRight'})` / `{key: 'ArrowLeft'}` instead of a click, proving the same wrap-at-both-ends behaviour is reachable via keyboard on the container itself.

**Explicitly out of scope, do not add:** no change to `carousel`/`indicatorWrapper` CSS or their gating logic, no Home/End/PageUp/PageDown key handling, no focus trap, nothing else. If you find yourself touching the media-query gate or the visual arrows/indicator split at all while doing this fix, stop — that's not what's authorized.

## After all five fixes, verify:
```
npx tsc --noEmit
npx vitest run overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia
npx vitest run overrides/app/components/ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts
npx vitest run overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts
npx eslint overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia
node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs
npm run test
```
All must be clean/green. Confirm via `git status --porcelain` that only the 4 existing Step 4 files show any diff (plus the pre-existing, unchanged 1-line theme/components/index.ts diff from earlier in Step 4) — nothing else. Do NOT stage or commit. Report exactly what changed per fix, and confirm the falsification-and-revert proof for Fix 1.
